recap.workouts:
Three pieces today and all three landed.

06:00 Supply — 87 minutes on the clock, average heart rate 120, peak 170, load 40, and you rated it a 4. Three AMRAP 8s at [FITNESS] with the runs conversational, which is exactly the call the plan asked for. That mattered more than usual today: the afternoon's measurement is only worth something if the morning in front of it looks like the mornings in front of the other five, and it did. You went in feeling low, and flagged nerve pain in the right leg tracing back to a metcon lift a week ago Monday. Worth saying plainly — you put a complete, well-judged day together on top of that.

Hypertrophy, upper push and triceps, the first full-volume session of the new block: all 13 prescribed sets landed at the prescribed loads. Incline DB press 70 for 11/10/9/9. Chest fly 40 on the cable for 15/15/15. Lateral raise 20 for 20/20/20. Triceps pushdown at the new 100 for 8/8/8. Chest 7, side delts 3, triceps 3 — every muscle exactly on its engine number.

CF10, 61 minutes, 34.6 km, 158.6 W average, load 46 against a planned 47, compliance 97.9 percent, paired cleanly to the planned session. The shape of it, read off the per-second trace:

Warm-up, minutes 0 to 15 — 148 W, heart rate walking up from 87 to the low 130s at a little over a beat a minute. Ordinary.

Zone 2 opens, minutes 15 to 20 — 168 to 170 W.

The reference block, minutes 20 to 30 — 164.5 W with a spread of 0.7 W across the whole ten minutes. That is as flat as this can physically be ridden, and it was the one thing today had to deliver. Heart rate settled at 134 after the first minute and finished at 133, so it went DOWN 1.4 beats across the block rather than up, and the power-to-heart-rate relationship was half a percent better in the back five minutes than the front five. Against a bike threshold heart rate of 159 you sat at 83 percent of it. Nothing about those ten minutes was work.

The rest of the Zone 2 hold, minutes 30 to 50 — up from 165 to 179 W by minute 40 and back to 165 by minute 50, averaging 172, heart rate 132 rising to 140 at minute 46. The rise is proportionate to the extra watts and the relationship holds.

Zone 1 tail, minutes 51 to 61 — 149 W, heart rate settling back into the low 130s.

Whole ride: 50.5 percent Zone 1, 48.1 percent Zone 2, zero Zone X, nothing above Zone 2 at any point, max heart rate 144. You said it felt better than expected and that the legs were very sore and tired afterwards — the trace backs the first half of that, and there is nothing anywhere in it that looks like a struggle.
recap.takeaways:
1) THE BLOCK LANDED, AND IT LANDED CLEAN. Ten minutes at 164.5 W with 0.7 W of spread, heart rate settled at 134 and finishing at 133, and the power-to-heart-rate relationship flat to slightly improving across it. That is the sixth observation in the 160-169 W bin and there is nothing wrong with it: no ragged power, no runaway heart rate, no early stop, 97.9 percent compliance. Confidence high — this is off the full per-second trace, not a summary. Consequence: proceed. There is nothing here to protect against.

2) ZERO ZONE X IN 61 MINUTES. Half the ride Zone 1, half Zone 2, nothing above at any point, the whole hour ridden at 83 percent of bike threshold heart rate. Week 13's premise is that last week broke on lost easy volume rather than on too much hard work, so the answer was more easy minutes and nothing added. Day one is exactly that shape. Keep it.

3) FULL VOLUME BACK AND ALL OF IT LANDED — 13 of 13 sets on an 80 percent volume step, six novel loads in the week and no reason yet to defend any of them. Chest fly swept 15/15/15 at 40, so the trigger fires: 45 on the next chest day. Triceps pushdown gave 8/8/8 at the new 100 — that is the floor of the range, not under it, so the banked bump stands and 100 is the working load. Incline press 11/10/9/9 holds 70; lateral raise has 3 of the week's 7 sets at 20 reps, and Friday's 4 decide the 25s.

4) TOMORROW'S RIDE HAS TO BE INDOORS, AND TODAY'S WORK DEPENDS ON IT. CCI3's four Zone 3 reps are what measure the Zwift FTP offset, and the verdict discards any offset older than three days. Ridden indoors on Zwift, today's ten minutes become a measurement. Ridden outside, they get collected and then dropped at verdict time — the same failure that has already cost four observations.
recap.tomorrow:
Tuesday. 06:00 Medical — 1 pause jerk plus 1 jerk, six singles on the 2:00 at 75 to 80 percent of your clean and jerk, so take the 75 end at about 146. Metcon [FITNESS], two rounds for time, burpees over the bar capped at 8 to 10 per interval. No lifting session tomorrow. Then CCI3 in the afternoon, 61 minutes: 5 minutes Zone 1, 10 minutes Zone 2, then 4 x (6 minutes Zone 3 at 222-248 W / 3 minutes Zone 1), 5 minutes Zone 2, 5 minutes Zone 1 — indoors on Zwift. The recoveries are half the work intervals, so these are built to be repeatable rather than maximal: set the number in the first 90 seconds of rep 1, then ride it four times. If rep 4 is not rep 1's wattage, rep 1 was wrong.

Signals to read: whether the legs that felt very sore and tired after today's ride have settled, whether the right leg stays quiet through the class and the warm-up, and how the first 90 seconds of rep 1 sits — parked at 222-248 W, or forced.

Feeling good and rep 1 settling on its own? Ride all four 6-minute reps as CCI3 writes them, toward the upper part of the band.

Legs still heavy, or the right leg talking? Take three honest 6-minute reps at the same 222-248 W and ride the fourth rep's time out easy — same 61 minutes, and the plan's own cut order names that exact reduction. Either version measures the Zwift offset, which is the one thing tomorrow has to deliver. Both are a good day's work.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
CAn4 — 90' on the bike: 10' Z1, then 6 × (2:30 Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 5:00 Z1), 30' Zone 2 @ 165–196 W, 5' Z1. Both bands are the post-CT31 numbers (FTP 236 W). No gym, no class — Saturday is bike only.

If readiness is still down in the twenties, either drop it outright or ride only the 30' Z2 tail — six Z4 reps is the single biggest block of hard time left in a week whose entire job was to deload. If you wake up genuinely normal, ride it as written and keep the recoveries as lazy as today's were.

Sunday is full rest either way. That part isn't negotiable.
